analysis.one_liner: CG Power makes power transmission and distribution equipment (transformers, switchgear) and industrial products (motors, drives, railway systems), and is now building a new semiconductor packaging (OSAT) business under Murugappa Group ownership.
analysis.whats_happening: The board meets on October 23, 2026 (4 days from now) to approve Q2 and H1 FY27 results. In Q1 FY27 (June quarter), consolidated revenue rose 14% to Rs 3,281 crore and consolidated PAT rose 15.5% to Rs 308 crore, while standalone PAT grew faster, up 27% to Rs 364 crore - the gap is because the new CG Semi semiconductor venture is still loss-making and drags on the consolidated numbers. Order book grew 45% YoY to Rs 17,333 crore. Separately, statutory auditor S R B C & CO LLP (an EY network firm) resigned effective August 14, 2026, replaced by Price Waterhouse Chartered Accountants LLP on August 19, 2026 - the company says this was to align with parent Tube Investments' auditor network, not a dispute.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a century-old electrical equipment maker now owned by the Murugappa Group, and it's also placing a large, capital-intensive bet on semiconductor chip packaging (CG Semi) backed heavily by government subsidies. The core electrical business is growing well and getting more profitable - standalone margins improved from 15.4% to 16.9%. But the semiconductor arm is still burning money, which is why profit growth looks slower once you consolidate the two. The stock trades at roughly 110x earnings, which only makes sense if CG Semi eventually becomes a real, profitable business rather than a cash drain - that's the open question here, not whether the core business is doing fine (it is).
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (June 2026): standalone revenue and EBITDA both up 27% YoY-ish range, with standalone EBITDA margin expanding to 16.9% from 15.4%; standalone PAT up 27% to Rs 364 crore. Consolidated EBITDA margin only inched up to 14.7% from 14.2%, and consolidated PAT grew a slower 15.5% to Rs 308 crore - the difference is CG Semi, which remains in investment/loss mode and is not yet comparable to a steady-state industrial business. Treat standalone-vs-consolidated gap as a structural feature now, not noise, until CG Semi turns the corner.
analysis.performance_read: No recent corporate action (splits were in 2006 and 2010, long before the current price history) distorts the recent numbers, so the stock's returns can be read at face value. On that basis they are strong: +117.8% over 3 years and +562.2% over 5 years, both far ahead of the Nifty (+17.9%/+25.1%) and peer ABB India (+77.8%/+288.8%). Over 1 year the stock is up 15.45%, which is well ahead of the Nifty (-10.81%) but behind ABB (+34.73%), and the stock is currently 12.7% below its July 2026 peak of Rs 976.5. Worth remembering: this entity's 24-year listing history includes a period under its previous promoter (Avantha Group) when a major fund-diversion scandal was uncovered around 2019 - the strong multi-year returns shown here are really a post-2020 story under new Murugappa Group ownership, not a continuous track record.
analysis.valuation_read: Expensive by a wide margin - P/E of roughly 110-113x and P/B of about 17x, against an electrical equipment peer median closer to 34x P/E and 4.3x P/B. Why it's expensive: strong current return ratios (ROE ~20%, ROCE ~28%), a debt-free balance sheet, a fast-growing order book (+45% YoY), and the market pricing in optionality from the CG Semi semiconductor project. Whether that's justified is a separate question - it depends entirely on CG Semi scaling into a profitable business rather than staying a capital sink; if execution slips, a multiple this far above peers has a lot further to fall than to rise.
analysis.growth_read: The core electrical equipment business is growing on both volume and margin - revenue up 14% YoY with standalone EBITDA margin expanding from 15.4% to 16.9%, a healthier combination than margin expansion on flat volumes. At the consolidated level, growth looks more muted because CG Semi's investment-phase losses are netted in; strip that out and the underlying industrial business is genuinely expanding, not just getting more efficient.
analysis.health_read: Profits are converting into healthy return ratios - ROCE near 28%, ROE around 20%, and a debt-to-equity ratio of effectively zero. The balance sheet is not financially stretched. The real risk here is business risk, not financial risk: CG Semi is a brand-new, capital-intensive semiconductor packaging venture (total project cost ~Rs 7,584 crore, roughly 65% covered by central and state government support) whose commercial viability is still unproven, having only started production at its Sanand facility in July 2026.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter Tube Investments of India (Murugappa Group) holds roughly 56-58%, with 0% pledged - a clean current picture. Context matters here: this company was previously controlled by the Avantha Group, under which a large accounting/fund-diversion scandal came to light around 2019, leading to a management overhaul before Murugappa Group took control in 2020. The August 2026 auditor change (EY-network firm resigning, Price Waterhouse appointed) is described by the company as routine alignment with the parent's auditor network, not a dispute - but given this company's fraud history, auditor transitions are worth watching rather than waving through. No marquee individual investor (e.g., the kind tracked for other multibagger stories) was found on the current register in available sources - not verified either way.
strengths: Order book up 45% YoY to Rs 17,333 crore as of Q1 FY27, giving revenue visibility
Standalone EBITDA margin expanded to 16.9% from 15.4% YoY
Debt-free balance sheet with ROCE ~28% and ROE ~20%
Zero promoter pledge under Murugappa Group control since 2020
watchpoints: Trades at ~110-113x earnings versus a peer median near 34x - priced for near-flawless execution
CG Semi remains loss-making/investment-mode, holding consolidated EBITDA margin to 14.7% versus 16.9% standalone

Statutory auditor changed in August 2026 (second auditor transition in the company's recent history) - company calls it routine, but worth tracking given the entity's 2019 fraud history under its previous promoter
Stock is 12.7% below its July 2026 peak of Rs 976.5, and 1-year return of 15.45% trails peer ABB's 34.73%
analysis.one_thing: The October 23, 2026 Q2/H1 FY27 results - specifically whether consolidated margins start closing the gap with standalone margins, and what management says about CG Semi's timeline to profitability - will be the clearest signal on whether the ~110x earnings multiple is earning its keep.
analysis.data_notes: Q1 FY27 standalone and consolidated figures were cross-checked across multiple independent sources (Outlook Business, Bajaj Broking, Sahi, Equitybulls, Business Upturn, ScanX) and were consistent. P/E estimates varied slightly between sources (106.55x market-cap-based from one broker site versus 112.67x from an aggregator) - reported as a ~110-113x range rather than a single precise figure. Could not verify the exact record date for the next dividend, or confirm/deny whether any well-known individual investor currently holds a stake - flagged as not verified rather than guessed.
